title: Every header chip has a slash command in the prompt
body:
Each session setting has a chip in coax's header (coax-3ca4b5). A click opens a picker for that setting, and a choice goes to the agent through `session/set_config_option`, or through `session/set_mode` for agents with only the older modes API. Today the prompt passes everything typed to the agent, slash commands included.

## Proposal

- Every chip gets a slash command typed in the prompt, named after the setting: `/mode`, `/model`, `/effort`, `/fast`, and so on, from the setting's name in the agent's config options.
- With a value, as in `/model sonnet` or `/mode plan`, coax applies it the way the picker does. The value matches a choice's name or value, ignoring case.
- With no value, the command opens that chip's picker.
- The model command keeps the picker's warning about rereading the conversation, and stays refused while the agent works.
- An unknown value lists the valid choices as a dim line and applies nothing.

## Open

- Name clashes. The agent advertises its own slash commands through `available_commands_update`, and some may share a name with a setting. Which one wins, and how the other stays reachable, is undecided.
- Whether a setting name with spaces or capitals turns into a command name by lowercasing it and joining it with `-`.
